country.name: Kosovo
country.tagline: The Rahovec valley's sunny slopes, once the source of a German supermarket red, rebuilding as a small wine country.

stats.note: Kosovo Ministry of Industry, Entrepreneurship and Trade: 3,405.54 ha of vineyard in 2024 (Rahovec 2,465 ha, Suharekë 575, Prizren 198, Gjakovë 77, Malishevë 65); 35 licensed wineries, three of which make about 70% of the wine.

country.overview:
Kosovo's vineyards are concentrated in the south-west, in the Dukagjin plain (Rrafshi i Dukagjinit) and especially around Rahovec (Orahovac in Serbian), which alone has about 2,465 of the country's 3,400 ha. The hills around Rahovec, at 300 to 600 m with around 276 sunny days a year, loamy and red soils and a ripening season from mid-July to mid-October, have grown grapes since antiquity. In the Yugoslav era the state winery at Rahovec shipped large volumes of soft red wine to West Germany; it was sold there under brands such as Amselfelder, German for 'blackbird field', the meaning of the Serbian name Kosovo Polje.

War in 1998 and 1999 and the loss of the German market left the sector in ruins. The old state winery was privatised in 2006 as Stone Castle, bought for €5.5 million by Albanian-American businessman Rrustem Gecaj; it has a capacity of 10 to 13 million litres and is one of the largest private wineries in the region. Today 35 licensed wineries operate, three of them making about 70 percent of the wine, alongside many small family cellars in Rahovec, Suharekë and Prizren. Main grapes include Vranac, Prokupac, Gamay, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Smederevka, Riesling and Chardonnay.

history.title: Rahovec's big winery
history.text: The Rahovec winery that became Stone Castle was founded in 1952; it grew into a major exporter of red wine to West Germany in the Yugoslav period.

history.title: War
history.text: The Kosovo war devastated vineyards and ended the German export trade.

history.title: Stone Castle privatised
history.text: The former state winery was privatised for €5.5 million and renamed Stone Castle; its capacity is 10 to 13 million litres.

country.classification: Kosovo regulates wine through its own wine law and a register of licensed producers; vineyard statistics are kept by region (Rahovec, Suharekë, Prizren, Gjakovë, Malishevë). No Kosovar wine names appear in the EU or UK geographical-indication registers as of 2026.
country.climate_soils: Continental with Mediterranean influence from the south-west; about 276 sunny days a year in Rahovec; loamy soils with some red soils; vineyards mostly at 300 to 600 m.

grapes.name: Vranac and Prokupac
grapes.note: Balkan reds that dominate the local blends.

grapes.name: Gamay, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon
grapes.note: International reds planted widely in the Yugoslav era.

regions.name: Dukagjin
regions.tagline: Rahovec, Suharekë and Prizren: the sunny south-western hills where nearly all of Kosovo's vines grow.
regions.summary: The Dukagjin plain and its rim of hills in south-western Kosovo contain almost the whole vineyard: Rahovec (about 2,465 ha), Suharekë (575 ha), Prizren (198 ha), Gjakovë (77 ha) and Malishevë (65 ha), as reported by the ministry for 2024. Rahovec town is the wine capital, home of Stone Castle and dozens of family cellars.
regions.history: Yugoslav-era Rahovec exported red wine to West Germany; war and the loss of that market shattered the industry, which has been rebuilding since 2000.
regions.terroir: Hillsides at 300 to 600 m with loamy and red soils; continental climate with Mediterranean air from the Drin valley.
regions.grapes: Vranac, Prokupac, Gamay, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Smederevka, Riesling, Chardonnay.
regions.styles: Mostly reds, some whites and rosé.
regions.classification: No GIs; statistics and licensing by region.

sites.name: Stone Castle, Rahovec
sites.text: Founded in 1952 as Rahovec's large wine combine, the winery was privatised in 2006 for €5.5 million and renamed Stone Castle. With 10 to 13 million litres of capacity and the ability to process about 70,000 tonnes of grapes a season, it is one of the largest private wineries in Europe.

sites.name: Rahovec
sites.text: Rahovec (Orahovac) is Kosovo's wine capital. Its municipality holds about 2,465 of the country's 3,400 ha of vineyard on sunny hills at 300 to 600 m, with many small family cellars alongside Stone Castle.
